To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the sectoral structure is constant in the balanced growth path of a resource-based economy with heterogeneous resource intensities, (ii) resource taxes have no impact except when the tax is varied over time, (iii) research subsidies and the sectorally differentiated provision of public goods are growth enhancing and provide a tool for structural policy, and (iv) the resource intensity of the economy increases with technical progress.

heterogeneity in resource use induces technical change to become biased towards resource-intensive activities and that this bias can be mitigated by research subsidies and the provision of public goods.

the heterogeneity of resource intensities induces technical change to have a positive bias towards resource-intensive sectors, which leads to a constant sectoral structure in the long run, and that sector-specific research subsidies and the sector-specific provision of productivity-enhancement public goods are effective tools for the structural policy of an economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications of resource intensities for growth and the implications of growth for resource use.
the long-term dynamics and the implications of resource intensities on technical change and growth.
the long-term implications of the resource intensity of production.

the dynamics of a resource-dependent economy are not necessarily driven by the resource constraint.
the sectoral heterogeneity of resource intensities has important implications for the long-term dynamics and the structure of the economy.
heterogeneity is a source of growth and that the provision of public goods can be used as a policy tool to influence growth.

heterogeneity in resource intensities has important implications for the long-run dynamics of an economy and for the effectiveness of policy measures.
